proof_checks.singleton: At S_1, A has deleted T, increasing its work against D=N(A) to \mu+4 and decreasing it against E=N(B) to \mu. B has work \mu+4 against D and \mu against E. Thus A and B have identical rows against all other views. For E, its original grid neighbors are outside D, and no opposite pair involving E has a cross intersecting {A,B}, so no label in E has an excess of 4 against any view. A single edit changes work by \pm s_v^2 \neq 0, so it strictly destroys all old minimum edges to untouched labels. To form a new minimum edge, it must reduce an existing excess by a perfect square. The only square excess is 4, requiring s_v=2. The only available subtotal-2 leaf is T. Deleting T reduces work only against A and B, and only views in D have the required \mu+4 excess against them. Thus, a once-edited view has at most two untouched minimum neighbors (A and B), and must belong to D.

proof_checks.double_editors: For the (2,2) partition, if A edits, it cannot supply new edges to D because its two positive squares cannot sum to -4. The other editor must resolve the surpluses in E, forcing it to be in E. But an editor in E cannot supply the needed edges to D without dropping the work of its ordinary grid neighbors below \mu (by deleting U and R). If A stays fixed, the two editors must resolve all 4 surpluses in E, forcing them to be diagonal neighbors of B. They must supply two new edges each to D. Achieving a net -8 or -20 requires the larger feature to be absent, which limits the decrease to at most two labels in D. For all other untouched labels, the larger feature is present, strictly increasing the work. Consequently, these editors lose all their old minimum edges and can only connect to the two labels in D and the other editor, capping their degree at 3 and failing the 4-regularity gate.
proof_checks.parity: The symmetric-difference work satisfies W_{ij} \equiv M_i + M_j \pmod 2, where M_i is the P1 depth moment. If the minimum were odd, the minimum edges would form a bipartite graph between even and odd M_i. A 4-regular bipartite graph requires an even number of vertices, but there are 25 views. Thus, the minimum must be even, forcing all M_i to share the same parity. Since the source event deletes T (subtotal 2, even), the parity of M_A is unchanged. Therefore, all views must preserve their parity, requiring an even number of odd-subtotal deletions per view. The archived 100-step witness perfectly reflects this: 19 views make 4 edits, 4 views (exactly E) make 6 edits, and 2 views (A and B) make 0 edits, preserving parity across all 25 views.
